claim_verdicts.evidence: Architecture: "The application controller is a Kubernetes controller which continuously monitors running applications" and "compares the current, live state against the desired target state (as specified in the repo)." Repo server is "responsible for generating and returning the Kubernetes manifests" (no image build anywhere in the component list). Runs as Pods: argocd-install.txt lists 6 deployment.apps + 1 statefulset.apps in argocd.

Getting Started (release-3.1): "kubectl create namespace argocd" / "kubectl apply -n argocd -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/argoproj/argo-cd/stable/manifests/install.yaml" (no --server-side). Upgrading overview: "kubectl apply -n argocd -f https://raw.githubusercontent.com/argoproj/argo-cd/<version>/manifests/install.yaml". deploy/argocd/install.yaml:1 "# Argo CD v3.1.16: an unchanged copy of manifests/install.yaml"; images quay.io/argoproj/argocd:v3.1.16. argocd-install.sh:14 creates ns, :16 applies.

Getting Started installs Argo CD from outside the cluster with kubectl (create namespace, apply install.yaml); no Argo CD component exists before that apply. argocd-install.sh:3 "Runs on the host, like scripts/k8s/"; :14 and :16 perform the apply.

argocd-install.txt: "3 customresourcedefinition.apiextensions.k8s.io", "6 deployment.apps", "8 service", roles/clusterroles, "1 statefulset.apps"; deployments applicationset-controller, dex-server, notifications-controller, redis, repo-server, server; statefulset argocd-application-controller. Lesson's output block matches the file's lines 1-2, 6-7 and 16-32 (elided lines marked '...').

argocd-install.txt: "applications app,apps argoproj.io/v1alpha1 true Application", plus applicationsets and appprojects. gitops-first-sync.txt:2 shows kubectl apply of staging-manual.yaml printing "application.argoproj.io/staging" (kubectl applies the new kind like a built-in one).

Architecture: "The repository server is an internal service which maintains a local cache of the Git repository holding the application manifests." "The application controller is a Kubernetes controller which continuously monitors running applications" and "compares the current, live state against the desired target state (as specified in the repo)."

Projects: "If unspecified, an application belongs to the `default` project, which is created automatically". Tracking strategies, branch: "Argo CD will continually compare live state against the resource manifests defined at the tip of the specified branch"; commit SHA: "the app is effectively pinned". Declarative Setup example uses project, source.repoURL/targetRevision/path, destination.server/namespace.
K8s: "...so that pods may reference `kubernetes.default.svc` as a DNS name for the local API server." Declarative Setup Application example: "destination: server: https://kubernetes.default.svc".

Declarative Setup: "All resources, including Application and AppProject specs, have to be installed in the Argo CD namespace". Applications in any namespace: "this feature has to be explicitly enabled and configured appropriately." staging-manual.yaml:11 "namespace: argocd".

Auto sync: "Argo CD has the ability to automatically sync an application when it detects differences", enabled by an automated policy under syncPolicy. The page does not literally state manual is default; execution settles it: gitops-first-sync.txt after applying staging-manual.yaml shows "staging: OutOfSync, Missing" with every resource OutOfSync until the script requests "== sync".

gitops-first-sync.txt lists only objects of envs/staging (SealedSecret/* exist only in staging's folder per gitops-repo.txt). gitops-repo.sh:54-58 copies only apps/staging.yaml ("Only staging's Application from apps/"); gitops-repo.txt ls-files: apps/staging.yaml is the only file under apps/.

git-server.yaml: Namespace git; Deployment gitea replicas: 1; volume data emptyDir at /var/lib/gitea; Service gitea port 3000; ROOT_URL http://gitea.git.svc:3000/. K8s volumes: "any reason, the data in the `emptyDir` is deleted permanently." Service names resolve via cluster DNS only.

gitops-repo.sh:56-59 copies envs/ and apps/staging.yaml from deploy/gitops/config-repo, then runs seal-secrets.sh, which adds envs/staging/sealed-*.yaml generated from .env (:46-48 "for envs/staging the SealedSecrets that scripts/devops/seal-secrets.sh makes from .env"). gitops-repo.txt:28-34 lists 7 sealed-*.yaml that are not in deploy/gitops/config-repo/envs/staging (Glob: 9 files, none sealed-*). Rest of the claim holds (user donhang, "private":false, only .yaml).

issues.text: Unfixed from r2. Explanation b says an agent pointed at `envs` "cannot tell staging's files from production's". For an Argo CD directory source that is not what happens: Directory docs: "By default, directory applications will only include the files from the root of the configured repository/path." `envs` holds only the folders staging/ and production/, so Argo CD would read no manifests. Key (a) and b being wrong are unaffected.
issues.quote: and an agent pointed at both cannot tell staging's files from production's
issues.fix: Replace that clause (en+vi) with: "But `envs` also holds production's folder next to staging's; the source should name exactly the folder of one environment, so only staging's manifests are compared with `donhang`." / "Nhưng `envs` còn chứa thư mục của production cạnh thư mục của staging; source nên ghi đúng thư mục của một môi trường, để chỉ manifest của staging được so với `donhang`." Do not add the recurse detail.
